not-yet.title: Worlds not yet taken over by one founder's line
not-yet.caption: For every iteration, the share of the worlds whose living, at the check after that iteration's game (every 25 iterations), still descend from more than one founder. Yellow: the 30 worlds of 10,000 tokens; blue: the 30 of 100,000. A world that died, or never got there, stays in the share. Where a line crosses one half is its median; the thesis of Experiment 10 expected the blue one to cross between the two grey lines.
not-yet.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in Chapter 9). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`. The 30 baseline runs `B1-10000-s001` … `B1-10000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 10,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 3,000 iterations each (every setting is listed in Chapter 10). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E02`.

**Data.** From the lineage analyses of Experiments 10 and 6 (`book/results/E10.json`, `book/results/E06.json`, `oneFounder` of every run).

1. For every run, the first check at which every living agent descends from one founder.
2. For every t, the share of runs whose first such check is later than t, or that have none.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py takeover`.

sizes.title: How long a takeover takes, by the size of the world
sizes.caption: For every world of Experiment 8 that lived to its end (green, or grey if all its living still came from more than one founder at its last check, at iteration 600, drawn there), and for the median of each set of 30 worlds (blue): the first iteration at which every living agent descends from a single founder. Both axes logarithmic. Dashed: what the two paces of the thesis predict, drawn through the median of the worlds of 10,000 tokens, 175 — a front, whose time grows with the width of the world (orange), and chance, whose time grows with the number of agents (red).
sizes.recipe:
**Runs.** the baseline worlds of Experiment 8, three seeds at each of ten sizes from 800 to 409,600 tokens, 600 iterations each (Chapter 42; `python3 gol_lab.py run E08`); and the two sets of 30 worlds above.

**Data.** From each run's frames, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `gol_store.read_frame(run, index)`; frame `2·t` is iteration *t* after reproduction and frame `2·t + 1` after the game.

1. For the runs of Experiment 8, `gol_analysis.lineage` of every run (kept as the book measure `lineage`): its `ancestor.oneFounder`.
2. Plot it against the run's tokens; the two sets of 30 as in the figure above.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py takeover`.

domains.title: Do lines of descent hold regions?
domains.caption: An agent's family at lag k is the genotype alive k iterations earlier from which its own genotype descends. For pairs of agents r steps apart — from breadth-first searches out of 100 agents drawn at random, at five moments of each world's settled life — the share that belong to the same family, divided by the share among any two agents of the world, for four lags; each line is the median over the worlds. Left: the 30 worlds of 100,000 tokens; right: the 26 of 10,000. Above 1, neighbours are kin more often than chance; where a line falls to 1 is how far a family reaches.
domains.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in Chapter 9). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`. The 26 surviving ones of the 30 baseline runs `B1-10000-s001` … `B1-10000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 10,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 3,000 iterations each (every setting is listed in Chapter 10). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E02`.

**Data.** From each run's frames, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `gol_store.read_frame(run, index)`; frame `2·t` is iteration *t* after reproduction and frame `2·t + 1` after the game.

1. At five moments t of each run (`book_chapters.space.moments`), read the frames from t − 200 to t and note every genotype's parent; for each lag k, climb from each living agent's genotype to one alive after the game of t − k.
2. Breadth-first searches out of 100 agents drawn at random (seed 51), to 30 steps; per r, the pairs and the pairs in one family; chance: Σ c(c − 1) / (n(n − 1)) over the families' counts c (`book_chapters.scale.domains`).

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py takeover`.

ten-small.title: One world of 100,000 tokens beside one of 10,000
ten-small.caption: For each of 24 of the viewer's statistics, its mean over iterations 500–1,499 in each world that lived to the end; the median of the 30 worlds of 100,000 tokens divided by the median of the 26 worlds of 10,000 — over the same iterations, though the small worlds ran on to 2,999. On logarithmic axes, so that half as much and twice as much lie equally far from 1; each bar rises from 1 or falls from it. Blue: shares and rates per agent; green: the shape of the network; orange: its distances; red: its largest single things; grey: totals. The dashed guides: no change; ×2.0, the factor by which the width of a world grows (tokens^0.30, Chapter 42); and ×11, the ratio of the agents.
ten-small.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in Chapter 9). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`. The 26 surviving ones of the 30 baseline runs `B1-10000-s001` … `B1-10000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 10,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 3,000 iterations each (every setting is listed in Chapter 10). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E02`.

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](../notes/frames-and-stats.md)).

1. For every run and statistic, the mean over the rows of iterations 500 to 1,499 (`phase` 1 for births, 2 for the rest; a ratio such as `edges/nodes` is taken row by row).
2. The median over each set's runs; the large set's divided by the small set's.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py takeover`.
